text:
maria: Quick Q — how are we standardizing cancellation for long-running streaming responses across SDKs? I noticed Node (AbortController) vs Go (context) differences. Goal: abort by user => close connection, server notified, no client-triggered retries. Thoughts?

lee: high level: agree on semantics. Abort = user-initiated stop, should not trigger retry. But we need server-side drain so GPU tasks aren't leaked. Can we have the server emit a 'client_cancel' event so we can audit/cleanup?

sam: Node note: typical pattern is: 
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ac.signal });
// streaming: read from res.body.getReader()
// to cancel: ac.abort(); // fetch throws DOMException 'The user aborted a request.'
```
In practice our fetch wrapper sometimes turns that into a generic network error and the retryer kicks in. We should mark client-abort so retryer no-ops.

nina: Python async: with httpx/asyncio we rely on task.cancel() which raises asyncio.CancelledError inside the coroutine. Sync httpx/requests don't have a first-class signal so we wrap in a background thread and set a flag — ugly. We should add an SDK-level CancelledByClient exception type to normalize.

maria: Go: context.WithCancel(ctx) cancels properly but the transport returns errors like "context canceled" or EOF depending on where cancellation happens. We need consistent mapping to CancelledByClient and ensure RetryPolicy sees it. Also need to handle cases where cancel happens during header exchange vs during streaming body.

dev-bot: created rfc: /docs/rfcs/cancel-handshake.md and issue #1421 to add tests + mapping. @lee @sam assigned. :sparkles:

sam: edge case: abort during initial headers (before body) — should we treat as non-idempotent/no-retry? My vote: yes, treat as user cancel and never retry. Otherwise clients could accidentally double-charge downstream ops.

lee: +1. Implementation idea: SDK attaches metadata on request object: { user_cancel: false } default. When AbortController/context signals, set user_cancel = true and surface CancelledByClient error. Retryer checks that flag.

nina: I'll open a PR to add CancelledByClient error and the mapping table:
- Node: DOMException name/message -> CancelledByClient
- Python: asyncio.CancelledError / httpx.ReadTimeout? -> CancelledByClient if caused by task.cancel()
- Go: context.Canceled / net errors containing "use of closed network connection" -> CancelledByClient
Will add unit tests that simulate socket RST and task.cancel().

maria: Logging/observability request: include request_id + event 'client_cancel' in the tracing payload so ops can slice out user-initiated cancels from infra incidents. Also prefer an enum for cancel reason: { user_abort, timeout, server_kill }

ops-bot: FYI — prod telemetry shows ~10% of streaming sessions ended with client-side cancel in us-west-2 over the last 24h. Tagging @eng-sre and @eng-runtime for follow-up.

sam: followup: also consider streaming backpressure: if client cancels due to slow chunks, do we send SIGPIPE vs RST? Need deterministic server handling so GPU work is reclaimed quickly. I'll add tests that force slow chunking.

lee: plan for next sprint:
- add CancelledByClient error class in each SDK
- propagate a user_cancel flag to retryer
- server to emit 'client_cancel' event in trace/logs
- tests: header-phase cancel, mid-stream cancel, slow-chunk cancel (socket RST)

nina: PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/999 — includes Node + Python mapping + unit tests.

maria: great. Can we also add a short note in changelog/docs that user-cancel won’t retry and will be surfaced as CancelledByClient? ops wants it in the runbook.

sam: will open doc PR for changelog + runbook after tests land.

maria: thanks everyone — assign follow-ups in the RFC issue. cc @eng-runtime @eng-sre for rollout checks.
